data.name: Luxor 3
data.detailed_description:
Um bravo e jovem Faraó, morto prematuramente por uma forte tempestade de areia e reencarnado pelos deuses como um escaravelho hábil, tem de lutar contra Set, o poderoso deus do caos, para libertar as essências de outros Deuses Egípcios contidas dentro de esferas coloridas mágicas.
Pára a fila das esferas enquanto elas viajam pelo labirinto juntando três ou mais. Chama os deuses, indicados pela cor, para libertar power-ups específicos e upgrades com moedas Ankh colecionadas durante o jogo. Liberta todos os deuses do cativeiro antes que eles cheguem à pirâmide no fim do caminho, ou tudo está perdido para sempre.
  • Música original, animação melhorada e ainda mais efeitos espetaculares
  • Sete modos únicos de jogo, incluindo cinco nunca antes vistos
  • Mais de 140 níveis de jogo de roer as unhas
  • Jogo dinâmico e desafiador com caminhos e entradas interligadas
  • Usa refletores para fazer combinações que de outra maneira seriam impossíveis
  • Power-ups melhorados, e ainda conjuntos de bolas e shooters para desbloquear
  • Novo nível de bónus introduzido

reviews.review:
'Luxor 3' is a classic Egyptian-themed marble-shooter puzzle game where you play as a reincarnated scarab battling the god Set to free trapped god essences by matching colored spheres before they reach the pyramids.

I remember playing it only for 30 mins when it came out, because back then the games were working through subscription system, and I didn't have money to buy them (I mean, back then we all pirated games). Back then I really wanted to play this game (it had new scarabs, power-up upgrades, and etc.), because it was a continuation of my favorite game, 'Luxor 2'. However, after finally buying it on Steam and playing, I realized this game doesn't really live up to the glory of 'Luxor 2'.

What I really love about this game is that it's somewhere between 'Luxor 2', when 'Luxor' was great, and newer installments, when 'Luxor' went downhill; so basically, this is the last good 'Luxor' game in the franchise. I really love "Crossing the Nile" mode, I could play it all day long. 'Luxor 3' also has statistics, but compared to 'Luxor 2', it diminished a lot: like there's no stats for each marble destroy, for each level wins/losses, for each power-up, and etc., there're only stats for each difficulty completed, global points, accuracy, and etc., that's all. Not much, but I'm still glad they didn't totally abandon the lifetime statistics. Also, I believe (I may be wrong) 'Luxor 3' uses real 3D maps. By "real" I mean not movies of 3D maps behind/under the marbles and PC, but the 3D map really exists on our screens. Graphics-wise, 'Luxor 3' is an upgrade.

Thanks God, this one doesn't rely on Flash, so this will work on newer systems, but this game has so many flaws that I can't really recommend it, but I have to.  Let's start with the obvious one: I really hate the crosshair, this must be the worst crosshair in any game I've ever played in my entire life, or even in gaming history; it's really weird, your second marble/shot is shown in a dot, but your first marble/shot over it in a shape like upside down "U". I swear, I have 99% accuracy in 'Luxor 2', and I almost always get 100% accuracy, except a few times when I'm in a hurry, or just miss, or in some maps where you have more chance of missing due to the layout, but in 'Luxor 3', I get 100% accuracy 50/50; that crosshair is confusing as hell. Why would you put first marble on a upside down U-shaped part of the crosshair when literally every crosshair in literally every game uses center dot for the main shot? Maybe if you never held a mouse in your hand, you'll have better time using this crosshair, but for anyone with legacy skill of FPS games, this crosshair will make their experience of this game uncomfortable. Speaking of uncomfortable, the physics in 'Luxor 3' is bad, and I mean it: you shoot a marble at a certain angle, where you know in 'Luxor 2 it would land there, but here it lands near it, ruining the marble train. Multicolored marble and recoloring power-ups (forgot their official names) have similar designs, I've missed good opportunities because of them many times than I would like to admit; it would be cool if the devs just used better design. Bonus levels are fun and chaotic, but getting 100% accuracy on them almost impossible (I know you don't even need to get 100% accuracy on them, because there's no such achievement for it in 'Luxor 3' unlike 'Luxor 2', but still). Also, don't like how marble train attaches itself when you break its middle part, this also confuses veteran players if they came from earlier 'Luxor' titles. Another problem is that the devs abandoned this game, too: they didn't implement Steam Cloud feature for this game, so if you want to keep your stats forever, you'll need to move your save file between your PCs. Surprisingly, 'Rockstar' is also lazy when it comes to this, they also don't have Steam Cloud for any of their games (from the very first 'GTA' till 'GTA V'), which is weird, because 'GTA' games was always popular because of their extremely detailed statistics; it really would be cool to save those stats forever.

In conclusion: 'Luxor 3' is a good gameif you are a fan of 'Luxor 2', and want to experience another 'Luxor' game, but 'Luxor 3' has TERRIBLE UX, I would say it lacks UX at all.
